title: II. Union of believers with God
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Notabilia: ye union stands as real not imaginary; outside it one can neither act well, enjoy true peace, nor be blessed; it does not wholly remove infirmities in this life yet covers and increasingly purges them; believers united toward God also share communion with one another. — II. Ye union belonging toward believers with God stands as that by which a human stands as joined toward Father, Son, and Holy Spirit through faith—mystically yet truly and most closely—so as toward abide in Him and be blessed forever.
pass_b_english: II. The union of believers with God is that by which a human is joined to Father, Son, and Holy Spirit through faith—mystically yet truly and most closely—so as to abide in Him and be blessed forever.

Notabilia: the union is real not imaginary; outside it one can neither act well, enjoy true peace, nor be blessed; it does not wholly remove infirmities in this life yet covers and increasingly purges them; believers united to God also share communion with one another.
source_text: II. Unio fidelium cum Deo est, qua homo Deo Patri, Filio et Spiritui Sancto, per fidem mystice quidem, vere tamen arctissime coniungitur, ut in eo maneat et beetur aeternum (Hos. 2:19-20; John 14:23; 17:21; Eph. 3:17; 1 Cor. 6:19). III. Notabilia: 1. Unio non est imaginaria sed vera—Deus venit, habitat, manet in homine. 2. Extra unionem homo neque bene agere neque vera tranquillitate frui neque beari potest (John 15:4-5). 3. Unio infirmitates in hac vita non omnino tollit, tamen tegit magis magisque purgat. 4. Quemadmodum fideles unum sunt cum Deo per Christum, ita inter se communionem bonorum habent.
